subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Pre-Mortem Analysis
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Pre-Mortem Analysis.

hook.text: Before starting a project, imagine it has failed. Now explain why. This is a pre-mortem, and it catches blind spots.

buildup.text: Gary Klein developed the technique. It gives people permission to voice doubts they would suppress in a positive.

discovery.text: Pre-mortems increase the number of identified risks by 30% compared to standard planning.

twist.text: The method works because it flips overconfidence. Instead of asking what could go wrong.

climax.text: Pre-mortems combine imagination with pessimism. They make risk visible before it becomes real damage.

punchline.text: Assume failure first, then prevent it. Pre-mortems catch what optimism hides.

quiz.question: How does a pre-mortem differ from standard risk planning?
options: It assumes the project has already failed and asks why, unlocking hidden concerns
